limitations: The bundle was generated from the canonical cluster checkout, not from the deployed clone's own object store, for the measured Lustre/pack reason above. Consequence: this is a recovery source for the pinned COMMIT and the deployed clone's REF SET, not a byte-image of that clone's object store. The pinned STATE is identified by HEAD + ref set + commit content, and all three are recorded here.

Reading the deployed clone with git is NOT a read-only act (DECISION-20260825 section 11.1): a git invocation there may write a lock into .git. Every read in this work set GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, and every tool output was written OUTSIDE the deploy tree.

The new freeze rule is preventive prose plus A-2(a) detection, not a mechanical guarantee. It is weaker than 'the tree is read-only' sounds: .git is writable by ruling, the owner may chmod the working tree back, and root ignores mode bits. What the arrangement gives is that any deliberate move leaves a trace in A-2(a) and A-2(f).

A-2(g) is scoped by the tool to tracked sources and their containing directories -- 1003 protected paths here. No A-2 claim in this receipt is phrased over the whole tree, and loose-object modes inside .git appear in no clause.
